A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ClimaQA/ClimaGen work. All 18 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable, and retained content can be matched across renaming, relocation and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM benchmark results, cloze-metric validation and automated-annotation experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds Gemini comparisons, ClimaQA-Silver evaluations, metric case studies and expert-rejection analyses.

M1.justification: ClimaGen retains the same generation, complexity evolution, screening, expert validation and GPT-4o-mini annotation procedures, including the confidence threshold and sampling rule. Generation prompts also match. Larger annotation samples and the additional evaluated comparator do not change the proposed framework.

E1.justification: The climate-textbook coverage, three QA forms, complexity levels, Gold/Silver datasets and Climate-Fever metric check are retained. Silver was already used for training. Its additional evaluation, the larger Gold sample and whole-book context comparisons change evaluation procedures within existing coverage; newly identifying the textbooks does not establish a corpus change.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds Gemini-1.5-Flash in default, source-book long-context and held-out-book long-context settings. All previous comparators remain. The rag-5/rag-13 and book/qa variants are renamed source/held-out and cp-held-out/ft-silver without becoming different methods.

E3.justification: Gold MCQs increase from 181 to 245, and the labeled MCQ annotation pool increases from 220 to 292 examples. v2 also introduces whole-textbook context evaluation and default-model testing on 200 Silver questions per task. These substantially extend evaluation design; existing metrics and LoRA training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of whether Silver preserves Gold's performance and difficulty patterns, detailed freeform/cloze metric case studies, and an expert-rejection error breakdown (Appendices A.2.2–A.2.3 and A.5.1). These materially expand diagnostic evidence beyond the retained context-window and annotation-validation studies.

E5.justification: The cloze-window error bars and three annotation train/test trials already appear in v1 and remain in v2. No additional seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: All 32 retained MCQ result rows change on the expanded test set; for example, GPT-4o source-RAG overall accuracy changes from 91.71 to 92.79. This is not a same-setting performance gain. Corresponding cloze scores and all retained freeform scores are unchanged. Gemini, Silver, case-study and rejection-distribution results add substantial new evidence.

T1.justification: The factual-accuracy smoothing and phrase-similarity equations retain the same operations. v2 explicitly names the logits and embeddings and revises their notation, without changing mathematical reasoning or adding assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain ClimaGen, Gold/Silver datasets, three QA forms with varying complexity, tailored evaluation metrics and comparisons highlighting RAG's benefits. The title's replacement of foundation models with question-answering models clarifies the LLM QA scope already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific qualifications: factual-accuracy scoring can reward irrelevant answers, Silver's difficulty differences may reflect small samples, and flawed seed contexts contribute to generation errors. These refine the existing interpretations and limitations. However, the new emissions case mischaracterizes the quoted Gemma response as predicting declining emissions.

D1.justification: v1 leaves its textbook sources unnamed and provides no concrete resource-access instructions. v2 identifies all 18 books and the five generation sources, supplies page/chunk counts and preprocessing details, and reports dataset/code locations. Its reproducibility statement also explains copyright restrictions, API requirements and expert-dependent variability. Existing prompts and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Bai and Wang QA survey, the Gemini 1.5 reference and citations identifying the textbook corpus. The related-work comparisons and positioning against existing scientific benchmarks and question-generation approaches otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and terminology become more explicitly focused on LLM question answering, the introduction gains application motivation, and a reproducibility statement is added. Appendices are reorganized around textbook documentation, experiments, training, prompts and annotation. Most existing explanatory prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts an ICLR layout with different margins, typography and figure placement, expands Table 3, and adds the textbook table, two Silver-results tables, source-distribution and rejection-distribution charts, and case-study displays. Figure 4 is restyled. Existing illustrations are retained, including v1's annotation Figure 6 as v2's Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially reduces v1's central provenance and reproducibility gap by identifying the corpus, source partition, preprocessing and resource-access locations. Silver comparisons and generation/metric failure analyses also make the benchmark's reliability easier to assess. One added case study misreads its quoted Gemma response, and uncertainty reporting remains limited, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in transparency and diagnostic evidence.
